name: Ecology Mapping
description:
Ecology mapping visualises the network of people, organisations, technologies, resources and relationships surrounding a design situation. Rather than examining a product or user in isolation, the map helps designers see the wider ecology in which experiences and outcomes are produced.

The emphasis is on relationships: who or what influences whom, what resources move through the system and where dependencies or tensions occur.
whenToUse: Use ecology mapping when a design challenge involves many interconnected actors or when focusing on a single user-product relationship obscures important influences.
steps: Define the situation or experience being mapped.
Identify relevant human and non-human actors.
Place the focal issue or experience on the mapping surface.
Add actors, organisations, technologies and resources around it.
Annotate important flows, dependencies, conflicts or exchanges.
Identify missing actors and indirect influences.
Examine the map for leverage points, tensions and questions requiring further research.
lookOutFor: A visually complex map is not necessarily an insightful map.
Avoid treating every connection as equally important.
The map reflects the knowledge and perspective of whoever created it; validate important relationships through research.

resources.citation: Tomitsch, M. et al. (2021). *Design. Think. Make. Break. Repeat*. BIS Publishers.
